terms.comment: The singular is the Vulgate’s and the Church’s; classical Latin has āra, and altāria, plural, for a high altar (Lewis & Short). In Orthodox speech “the altar” is often the whole sanctuary behind the iconostasis, and the table itself the holy table.

terms.gloss: an altar (the classical word, of pagan altars)
the Lord’s table; the holy table
evidence: Vulg. 1 Cor. 10.21: mēnsae Dominī participēs esse

phrases.latin: tantum illud vōs rogō, ut ad dominī altāre meminerītis meī, ubiubi fuerītis
phrases.english: only this I ask of you, that you remember me at the Lord’s altar, wherever you may be

phrases.latin: Et introībō ad altāre Deī, ad Deum quī laetificat juventūtem meam.
phrases.english: And I will go in to the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth.

sources: Lewis & Short: altaria · Lewis & Short: ara · Lewis & Short: mensa
